response.rationale: C1 is the most complete diagnosis: it includes the apocrine papillary tumor architecture and myoepithelial-lined circumscription of R2, and adds the decisive atypical features of multilayered epithelium, mitotic figures, and necrosis without dermal invasion. R2 is a strong runner-up but omits these atypical features. R5 addresses only adjacent congophilic dermal deposits and does not explain the main tumor; R1 relies only on childhood duration and lacks sebaceous/verrucous histology.

rejected.why: Only explains the adjacent congophilic dermal deposits; does not account for the circumscribed apocrine papillary tumor or p63-positive myoepithelial layer.
Only supports childhood duration; the histopathology shows an apocrine papillary neoplasm rather than sebaceous/verrucous features of nevus sebaceus.
